Common/Hardware/Weapons/_Bullets/PD_.416.contents: Interdictor standard projectile: drag, gravity, material and linked damage curves.

findings.question: Which linked curve is the site's damage curve, and how do the other curves differ?
findings.conclusion: Four linked curves. Two health curves peak at 150 (120-150 m) and fall to 62; their falloff ends differ (170 m in Field_6008eb31, 175 m in Field_2ad7e688). Two armor curves peak at 102.5. The GRX named registry supplies TweakableDamageCurve (175 m) and TweakableArmorDamageCurve; the site uses the 175 m health curve. Runtime curve selection is not decoded. Curve GUIDs also appear in TweakablesConfig.

findings.question: Where did the 1.4.3.0 Interdictor damage and falloff changes land?
findings.conclusion: Both curves changed here, not in the weapon blueprint. Curve ba0c9abc moved from 100m/80, 120m/150, 150m/150, 175m/62, 200m/62 to 100m/80, 120m/100, 160m/100, 180m/80, 200m/80, matching the patch notes for minimum damage 62 to 80, sweet spot 150 to 100 and sweet spot range 120m to 160m. Curve ea2b0ed0 went flat to 100 at every listed distance, matching the note about armour damage in REDSEC becoming 100 regardless of hit location or distance. The armour role of the second curve is inferred from the patch-note wording, not decoded. DesertTechHTI_WB itself changed only muzzle-flash FX references.

findings.question: What are the full 1.4.3.0 Interdictor damage values for the site?
findings.conclusion: The curve stores distance and damage together, so both are available: Field_3901db14 is the distance and Field_42fc0f5e is the damage at it. 1.4.3.0 is 100m/80, 120m/100, 160m/100, 180m/80, 200m/80, replacing 100m/80, 120m/150, 150m/150, 175m/62, 200m/62. The asset keeps the curve twice, as a point list and a flat array; in 1.4.2.5 the two disagreed on the fourth distance (170 in the point list, 175 in the flat array, and the site used 175), and in 1.4.3.0 both agree on 180. PD_.416Barrett_Match carries the same change.

findings.question: What is Field_440ed7fa, which moved from 0 to 0.067 on the ScorpionEvo3 and the Skorpion in 1.4.3.0?
findings.conclusion: Traced 15 September 2026. The field is a duration in seconds quantised to whole 1/60 s frames: all 15 distinct values across 64 weapon blueprints are exact frame counts (4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 16, 18, 22, 24, plus 0), and the apparent error is only 3-decimal rounding of n/60. It is not the rate of fire. GRX_Weapons names RateOfFire and RateOfFireForSingleFire separately, and they disagree with this field on at least nine weapons: the 590A1 holds 0.4 against a 60/RateOfFire of 0.033, the DP12 0.4 against 0.167, the Desert Tech HTI 0.4 against 0.2, and the ACE32, APC10, BREN3, HK433, EF88 and HK417A2 all sit one or two frames above their cadence. Where the two do agree the field equals 60/RateOfFire rounded to a frame. It is not a named registry leaf either: matching its per-weapon values against every GRX_Weapons leaf found only CustomZeroingDelay at 7 of 12 weapons, and that leaf is a constant 0.4 on the DMRs where it disagrees. Reading: a frame-quantised timing window that tracks cadence but is clamped, most likely an animation or input window rather than the cadence itself. The 1.4.3.0 change put the ScorpionEvo3 and the Skorpion on 0.067, four frames and the smallest value in use, from 0. Still not semantically named, so it is not applied to the site, and the site does not model such a window. Not identified; do not apply to the site. A survey of every _WB in the 1.4.2.5 export shows Field_440ed7fa is a per-weapon time-like value that tracks weapon class: 0.4 on the DP12, 590A1, Desert Tech HTI and L115A3, 0.3 on the M1014, 0.15-0.167 on the M18 and G22, 0.117-0.134 on the G3A4, ARA DMR and Five-Seven, 0.084-0.1 on assault rifles and carbines, and 0 on the KSG, ScorpionEvo3 and Skorpion. It is close to a shot interval but does not match site RPM consistently: the M1014 at 0.3 gives exactly 200 rpm and the AK-205 at 0.084 gives 714 against a site 720, but the L85A3 at 0.1 gives 600 against a site 635. The neighbouring Field_52a8ad43 is a constant 0.067 on every weapon, so 0.067 is the family floor. The 1.4.3.0 change therefore reads as two fast-firing weapons moving from unset to the floor value, not as a cadence edit. A trace against a named registry entry is needed before any site use.
